exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With Sine or Cosine Trigonometric Functions

question.explanation:
We know that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} ( \sin x ) = \cos x.$ Applying this formula, we have

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac {2\sin x}{3} +\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right) \\[5pt] & =\dfrac {2\cos x}{3} +\dfrac{3x^2}{3}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {2\cos x}{3}+x^2. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With the Tangent Trigonometric Function

question.text: Calculate the instantaneous rate of change of the function $f(x) = 6x - \tan x$ when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}.$
question.explanation:
The instantaneous rate of change when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is given by the value of the derivative $f'(x)$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}.$

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (\tan x) = \sec^2 x$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (6x) = 6.$ We get \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(6x - \tan x \right) \\[5pt] & = 6 - \sec^2 x. \end{align}

Evaluating at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3},$ we get

\begin{align} f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) & = 6 - \sec^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \\[5pt] & = 6 - \left(\dfrac{1}{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}\right)^2 \\[5pt] & = 6 - \left(\dfrac{1}{1/2}\right)^2 \\[5pt] & = 6 - 4 \\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align}

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change is $\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{2}.$

question.text: Calculate the instantaneous rate of change of the function $f(x) = 4x - \tan x$ when $x = 0.$
question.explanation:
The instantaneous rate of change when $x = 0$ is given by the value of the derivative $f'(x)$ at $x= 0.$

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (\tan x) = \sec^2 x$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (4x) = 4.$ We get

\begin{align} f'(x) &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(4x - \tan x \right) \\[5pt] &= 4 - \sec^2 x. \end{align}

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we get \begin{align} f'(0) &= 4 - \sec^2(0) \\[5pt] &= 4 - \left(\dfrac{1}{\cos(0)}\right)^2\\[5pt] &= 4 - \left(\dfrac{1}{1}\right)^2 = 4 - 1 \\[5pt] &= 3. \end{align}

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change is $\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{3}.$
